operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 provides that the Board of the Foreign Service and the Board of Examiners for the Foreign Service, established by EO 11264, shall exercise for Foreign Service information officers the functions that order delegated to them for Foreign Service officers, and that the Boards shall perform such further functions for United States Information Agency personnel as the Director may delegate. EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) revoked only Sections 1, 3 and 5 of EO 11434, so Section 2 survived that order, although Sec. 10(h) revoked Part III of EO 11264 (the Board of Examiners) effective 1981-02-15; that partial revocation reaches half of what Section 2 refers to and is listed as a later event. The Board of the Foreign Service (Part II of EO 11264) continued, and Section 2 with it, until EO 12363 (signed 1982-05-21; 47 FR 22497, Federal Register of May 25, 1982) said in its Sec. 3: "Executive Order No. 11264 of December 31, 1965, as amended, is revoked." EO 12363 states no later effective date, so the end is recorded as its signing date, 1982-05-21. Section 2 has no object once EO 11264, the instrument that established both Boards and delegated the functions Section 2 extends, was revoked in its entirety. No held source shows Section 2 extinguished earlier by the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (effective 1981-02-15): EO 12292, the order that conformed existing orders to that Act, left Sections 2 and 4 of EO 11434 unrevoked. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 amends Section 21 of EO 11264: it deletes the United States Information Agency from the list in subsection (b)(2), adds a new paragraph (b)(3) for two United States Information Agency officials designated by the Director, and conforms subsection (d). Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. The parent here is Section 21 of EO 11264 (Part II, the Board of the Foreign Service), which EO 12292 did not revoke (Sec. 10(h) revoked only Part III); Section 4 of EO 11434 was left unrevoked by Sec. 10(i). EO 12363 (signed 1982-05-21; 47 FR 22497) said in its Sec. 3: "Executive Order No. 11264 of December 31, 1965, as amended, is revoked." and states no later effective date, so the end is recorded as 1982-05-21. The amendment is a rewrite of part of a section that no longer existed after that date, and the Board it concerned was replaced by the Board of the Foreign Service established by Sec. 9 of EO 12293, as added by Sec. 1 of EO 12363. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 5 makes the order effective as of August 20, 1968 and authorizes the Secretary of State and the Director of the United States Information Agency to make rules and regulations under the order effective on or after that date. EO 12292 (signed 1981-02-23; 46 FR 13967, Federal Register of February 25, 1981), Sec. 10(i), revokes "Sections 1, 3, and 5 of Executive Order No. 11434 of November 8,1968;", and Sec. 11 says "This Order shall be effective as of February 15,1981." The revocation is therefore recorded as effective 1981-02-15, the stated effective date, not the signing date 1981-02-23. Sec. 10(i) names this section expressly; the effective date is a starting date and the rule-making authorization falls with the order's other provisions. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

research_rationale:
EO 11434 (signed 1968-11-08; 33 FR 16485, Federal Register of November 13, 1968) deals with the administration of the Foreign Service personnel systems: policies and regulations (Sec. 1), the Boards established by EO 11264 (Sec. 2), the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System (Sec. 3), an amendment of Section 21 of EO 11264 (Sec. 4) and its effective date (Sec. 5). EO 12292 (effective as of 1981-02-15) revoked Sections 1, 3 and 5; Sections 2 and 4 survived until EO 12363 revoked EO 11264 on 1982-05-21, which is the latest first end and so the whole-order end. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is the later formal revocation. The held OFR notes "Revoked in part by: EO 12292" and "Revoked by: EO 12553" are both reconciled in this claim, and EO 12107 (amendment) is a later event.

Executive Order 13322 of December 30, 2003
Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the laws cited herein, 
it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Statutory Pay Systems. The rates of basic pay or salaries of 
the statutory pay systems (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 5302(1)), as adjusted 
under 5 U.S.C. 5303(b), are set forth on the schedules attached hereto and 
made a part hereof: 
(a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5332(a)) at Schedule 1; 
(b) The Foreign Service Schedule (22 U.S.C. 3963) at Schedule 2; and 
(c) The schedules for the Veterans Health Administration of the Department 
of Veterans Affairs (38 U.S.C. 7306, 7404; section 301(a) of Public Law 
102–40) at Schedule 3. 
Sec. 2. Senior Executive Service. The ranges of rates of basic pay for senior 
executives in the Senior Executive Service, as established pursuant to 5 
U.S.C. 5382, as amended by section 1125 of Public Law 108–136, are set 
forth on Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a part hereof. 
Sec. 3. Executive and Certain Other Salaries. The rates of basic pay or 
salaries for the following offices and positions are set forth on the schedules 
attached hereto and made a part hereof: 
(a) The Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5311–5318) at Schedule 5; 
(b) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Congress (2 U.S.C. 31) 
at Schedule 6; and 
(c) Justices and judges (28 U.S.C. 5, 44(d), 135, 252, and 461(a), section 
140 of Public Law 97–92, and Public Law 108–167) at Schedule 7. 
Sec. 4. Uniformed Services. Pursuant to section 601(a)–(b) of Public Law 
108–136, the rates of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 203) for members of 
the uniformed services, as adjusted under 37 U.S.C. 1009, and the rate 
of monthly cadet or midshipman pay are set forth on Schedule 8 attached 
hereto and made a part hereof. 
Sec. 5. Locality-Based Comparability Payments.
(a) Pursuant to sections 5304 and 5304a of title 5, United States Code, 
locality-based comparability payments shall be paid in accordance with 
Schedule 9 attached hereto and made a part hereof. 
(b) The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take such 
actions as may be necessary to implement these payments and to publish 
appropriate notice of such payments in the Federal Register. 
Sec. 6. Administrative Law Judges. The rates of basic pay for administrative 
law judges, as adjusted under 5 U.S.C. 5372(b)(4), are set forth on Schedule 
10 attached hereto and made a part hereof. 
Sec. 7. Effective Dates. Schedule 8 is effective on January 1, 2004. The 
other schedules contained herein are effective on the first day of the first 
applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2004.

research_rationale:
EO 13322 (signed 2003-12-30; 69 FR 231, Federal Register of January 2, 2004) is the 2004 federal pay-adjustment order. Its Sec. 1 to 6 state the pay schedules (statutory pay systems, Senior Executive Service, executive and other salaries, uniformed services, locality payments, administrative law judges), Sec. 7 gives their effective dates and Sec. 8 supersedes EO 13282 as amended by EO 13291. EO 13332 (signed 2004-03-03; 69 FR 10891) says in its Sec. 8 that "Executive Order 13322 of December 30, 2003, is superseded." The end is recorded as 2004-03-03 with the later schedule-effective dates disclosed. The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR and the OFR order catalog) are used only for the coverage each states; none yields an earlier ending instrument, and EO 13332 is the only instrument that ends this order.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 13332 contains no savings clause for EO 13322, but it makes its own schedules effective on the same dates as this order's: "Schedule 8 is effective on January 1, 2004." and "The other schedules contained herein are effective on the first day of the first pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2004." Pay for pay periods before the supersession was earned under the schedules of EO 13322 or of its replacement and is a completed historical consequence, and the supersession of EO 13282 in Sec. 8 of this order is a completed effect; no continuing independent command of EO 13322 survives the supersession.
